skill.name: mermaid
skill.description: Guides creation of readable Mermaid diagrams for GitHub, with styling that works in light and dark modes.
skill.summary: Create clear, GitHub-compatible Mermaid diagrams with reusable styling and layout guidance.
skill.author: BfdCampos

security_audit.summary: One medium-severity concern is confirmed: the preview workflow uses npx with automatic confirmation and no package version pin. All other detections are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, Mermaid examples, benign metadata, and optional Mermaid Live links.

remediation.issue: The preview command downloads and executes an unpinned Mermaid CLI package through npx with automatic confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Pin an audited Mermaid CLI version and remove `-y`, or require explicit user approval before any package download and execution.

content.value_statement: Complex Mermaid diagrams can become unreadable or render poorly across GitHub themes. This guide provides tested syntax, styling patterns, layout techniques, and preview steps.
actual_capabilities: Creates flowchart structures with nodes, subgraphs, links, and directional layouts.
Applies dark fills, light strokes, and white text for cross-theme readability.
Uses GitHub-compatible labels, line breaks, shapes, and subgraph syntax.
Provides reusable color pairings and class definitions for consistent styling.
Guides rendering and visual review with Mermaid CLI or Mermaid Live.
Diagnoses common layout and syntax problems through documented correction patterns.
limitations: Focuses on flowcharts and does not cover every Mermaid diagram type.
Does not guarantee identical rendering across Mermaid versions or hosting platforms.
Requires users to preview and refine diagrams when automatic layout produces tangled edges.
The optional CLI preview command downloads an unpinned package unless the user pins a version.

use_cases.title: Document a pull request architecture
use_cases.description: Convert component interactions into a readable GitHub flowchart with grouped services, clear arrows, and theme-compatible styles.

use_cases.title: Explain a technical workflow
use_cases.description: Structure a process into concise stages and decisions for maintainable repository documentation.

use_cases.title: Map a data pipeline
use_cases.description: Show sources, transformations, storage, and outputs while keeping cross-system links easy to trace.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic flowchart
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a simple Mermaid flowchart for [process] with [steps]. Use rounded nodes, clear arrow labels, and styling readable in GitHub light and dark modes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Starting a new diagram from a short process outline.

prompt_templates.title: Convert process notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this process description into a GitHub-compatible Mermaid flowchart: [description]. Group related steps, quote subgraph labels, and use clear start and end nodes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Transforming existing prose into structured documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an existing diagram
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Mermaid diagram: [diagram]. Simplify tangled links, shorten labels, group related nodes, and apply dark fills with light strokes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Repairing a valid diagram that is difficult to read.

prompt_templates.title: Design a complex architecture view
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Mermaid architecture flowchart from [requirements]. Use directional lanes, minimize crossing edges, separate concerns with subgraphs, and explain any omitted secondary relationships.
prompt_templates.scenario: Creating an advanced diagram with several components and dependencies.

output_examples.input: Show how a user request passes through an API, validation service, database, and response handler.
output_examples.output: A top-down flowchart groups processing services, distinguishes the database shape, labels success and failure paths, and uses theme-compatible colors.

output_examples.input: Improve a deployment diagram with long labels, filled subgraphs, and many crossing arrows.
output_examples.output: A left-to-right diagram uses short multiline labels, transparent subgraphs, directional lanes, and fewer secondary links for clearer routing.

output_examples.input: Document a data pipeline from event collection through transformation and warehouse loading.
output_examples.output: A staged pipeline diagram groups ingestion, processing, and storage while using consistent styles and traceable arrows between each stage.

best_practices: Preview every diagram in the target renderer and revise unclear automatic layouts.
Keep the primary flow prominent and move secondary relationships into prose when links become crowded.
Use consistent class definitions, transparent subgraphs, quoted labels, and theme-compatible color contrast.
anti_patterns: Do not assume syntactically valid Mermaid is visually readable without rendering it.
Do not use light node fills or colored subgraph backgrounds that fail across GitHub themes.
Do not add every possible relationship when secondary edges obscure the main flow.

faq.question: Which Mermaid diagrams does this skill support best?
faq.answer: It focuses on flowcharts for architecture, processes, systems, and data pipelines in GitHub Markdown.

faq.question: Will diagrams work in GitHub light and dark modes?
faq.answer: The recommended dark fills, light strokes, white text, and transparent subgraphs are designed for both themes.

faq.question: Does the skill render diagrams automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides a Mermaid CLI command and a Mermaid Live link for user-controlled previewing.

faq.question: Why should subgraph labels be quoted?
faq.answer: Quoted labels with spaces avoid common Mermaid parsing errors and improve consistency.

faq.question: How should multiline node labels be written?
faq.answer: Use HTML line breaks in labels because escaped newline characters can render as literal text.

faq.question: Can Font Awesome icons be used?
faq.answer: GitHub Mermaid rendering does not reliably support them, so the guide recommends text and standard node shapes.
